newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: "Dirty war" general to ignore Spanish summons.
newsitem.headline: "Dirty war" general to ignore Spanish summons.

text.p: One of the generals who waged Argentina's infamous "dirty war" against leftist rebels said on Saturday he would ignore a summons issued by a Spanish judge to testify about the disappearance of Spaniards in Argentina.

"I don't think I will be arrested if I don't show up to testify before that Spanish judge," said Gen. Antonio Bussi, the elected governor of the northern province of Tucuman, according to the state-run Telam news agency.

Earlier this week, Spanish high court judge Baltasar Garzon, who is investigating the disappearance of more than 400 Spaniards in Argentina during the 1976-83 dictatorship, called on 101 members of the Argentine armed forces to give evidence about the "dirty war" in which thousands vanished without trace.
The attorneys who filed the suit in Madrid said they would seek international arrest warrants through Interpol if the accused refused to give testimony.

But Bussi, who as de facto governor of Tucuman under the military regime played a key role in the so-called "dirty war," said he would not go to Spain because the case had already been tried in Argentina.
The main military chiefs who directed the campaign of kidnapping, torture and murder against left-wing rebels were tried and imprisoned in 1985 and later pardoned and freed in 1989.
"In Argentina sanctions have been handed down and complied with, so this question is closed," Bussi said according to Telam.
